                                      Project Number 58481


RULEMAKING TO IMPLEMENT                       §       PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION OF
LARGE LOAD INTERCONNECTION                    §       TEXAS
STANDARDS UNDER PURA §37.0561                 §




                    Comment from the Hood County Clean Air Coalition

                                         Initial Comments
The Hood County Clean Air Coalition appreciates the opportunity to offer our comments
associated with Project Number 58481 that refers to the draft rules to implement large load
interconnection standards under PURA. We appreciate the PUCT taking these important steps to
provide draft rules to implement large-load interconnection standards. These rules are needed
expediently.

The Hood County Clean Air Coalition has concerns about projects being proposed below the
level of 75 MW to avoid the draft rule requirements. A lower threshold of 25 MW might be a
better level to bring more projects under the rule requirements and prevent smaller projects being
aggregated to avoid the requirements. There are also considerations that may be needed to
address the different size projects as a tiered system. Most of the projects proposed in and
around Hood County are 400 MW or larger. These draft rules address 75 MW, larger 250 MW,
or greater projects. There may be a need to address the progressively larger projects that are
larger than 500 MW and impose larger costs on these to address the higher interconnection costs
and greater expenses related to the required studies for these projects.

With how fast these projects are moving, would it be possible for these requirements to be
retroactive to include large-load customers already permitted, but not built, before these rules are
implemented? Is there a way to bring the projects that are not interconnected to the grid under
similar requirements as these proposed rules in the event they are later interconnected? Would
these rules apply to those projects if they seek interconnection later?



                                 Responses to Specific Questions



   1. Should the commission define parameters for determining whether a large load customer
      is pursuing a substantially similar interconnection request? If so, how should the
      commission define those parameters?
    Yes, the commission should define parameters for determining whether a large load
   customer is pursuing a substantially similar interconnection request. As some of these
   proposed projects are speculative, it would be beneficial to have as much information as
   possible to know upfront exactly what projects are being considered and help identify if
   they are duplicate or if they are not likely to happen.

2. Proposed subsections (c)(3), (e) (3), and (h)(3) require the disclosure of specific
   information related to a substantially similar request for interconnection and allows a
   large load customer to anonymize competitively sensitive details. Should the commission
   list what is and is not competitively sensitive (e.g., load zone is not competitively sensitive
   information)? If so, what information should and should not be considered competitively
   sensitive such that the interconnecting utility and ERCOT can identify whether there is a
   duplicate request, or a request is unlikely to materialize?

   Yes, the commission should list what is and is not competitively sensitive information.
   At least the load zone information and the general location should not be considered
   competitively sensitive to allow the interconnecting utility and ERCOT to identify
   whether there is a duplicate request or a request that is unlikely to materialize.

3. Should the commission require a large load customer to notify the interconnecting
   electric utility and ERCOT of any change to information that is initially disclosed in
   response to this rule or only material changes to the information disclosed? If only
   material changes, how should “material change” be defined?

   Yes, the commission should require a large load customer to notify interconnecting
   electric utilities and ERCOT of any material change to information that is initially
   disclosed in response to this rule. “Material change” should include load size and
   location.

4. Proposed subsection (k)(1) authorizes an interconnecting electric utility to refund 20% of
   a large load customer’s security after energization and ratably as the large load customer
   meets the milestones identified in the customer’s schedule for phased energization of it’s
   contracted load. Should the commission standardize the rate for refund for reaching
   milestones identified in the customer’s schedule for phased energization (e.g., 20% for
   each year of operations until the full amount of security is refunded)? If so, how should
   the commission standardize the refund?

   Yes, a standardized rate for refund for reaching milestones identified in the customer’s
   schedule for phased energization with the 20% per year of operation being reasonable.
 5.    Are changes to the commission’s other substantive rules necessary to align with this
     rulemaking? If so, what changes need to be made to which rules?

     As mentioned in the initial comments, consideration of lowering the threshold to 25 MW
     for a large load customer definition may help prevent projects coming in as an aggregate
     of several smaller projects to avoid these rules may be beneficial. Including projects that
     will be independent of the grid in these rules if they decide to interconnect later.



     Dated: December 17, 2025

                                                          Respectfully submitted,



                                                          Hood County Clean Air Coalition
                                                          P.O. Box 743
                                                          220 North Travis Street
                                                          Granbury, Texas 76048
           Executive Summary of Hood County Clean Air Coalition Comments



•   Recommend consideration of a lower threshold of 25 MW for the definition of a large
    load customer.
•   Tiered rate consideration for the study fee and financial commitments with larger
    projects subject to higher fees. The rules state that 75 MW-250 MW customers are to pay
    a study fee not less than $114,000 and projects over 250 MW customers are required to
    pay a study fee not less than $314,000. Some of the proposed projects are 400-950 MW.
    We would suggest a greater fee for these very large projects to create a tiered system.
•   Inclusion of projects that are permitted but have not started construction. With how fast
    the development of these large load customers is moving, many in our area are already
    permitted and set to begin construction in the coming months. In hopes that these rules
    would apply to them as well, we suggest that those large load customers be included.
•   Response to question 1 is that we agree the commission should define parameters for
    determining whether a large load customer is pursuing a substantially similar
    interconnection request to help identify if any projects are duplicate or are just
    speculative.
•   Response to question 2 is that we agree that the commission should list what is and is not
    competitively sensitive information and that load zone information and general location
    should be included in this information to identify duplicate requests or speculative
    requests.
•   Response to question 3 is that the commission should require large load customers to
    notify interconnecting electric utilities and ERCOT of any material change to
    information that is initially disclosed in response to this rule. “Material change” should
    include load size and location.
•   Response to question 4 is yes that a standardized rate for refund for reaching milestones
    identified in the customer’s schedule for phased energization with the 20% per year of
    operation is reasonable.
•   Response to question 5 is asking for consideration of lowering the threshold to 25 MW
    for a large load customer definition to help prevent projects coming in as an aggregate of
    several smaller projects to avoid these rules. Also, consideration of including customers
    who are independent of the grid in these rules if they decide to interconnect later.
